I've put together a plan for Nadia Rahman's hire (event seq 1, case-18026938), and nothing needs a human decision. Before planning I re-checked the investigator's findings. As of 2026-11-02 00:24 the event feed still holds only seq 1, and her Workday record hasn't changed (E1023, Software Engineer, cost center CC-1000, manager Jordan Carter, no work email yet). She starts 2026-11-04, about two days away.

The plan works around that start date:
- **Now:** create her Finance profile and order her equipment, since neither gives her access. Her expense approver will be her manager, Jordan Carter, because no approver is set anywhere else. Once the order is confirmed in ITSM, mark the "Provision equipment" task complete.
- **On or after 2026-11-04:** Identity waits for the start date, then creates her account (nadia.rahman@example.com) and adds her three standard access groups (All-Staff, VPN-Users, Eng-Git). None of them are privileged and they don't conflict with each other.
- **After the account exists:** write her email back to Workday and confirm it took effect. Only then mark the "Create accounts and email" task complete.

Every create step first checks whether the thing already exists and uses a key based on the case ID, so a retry can't create duplicates. Before acting on the start date, Identity re-reads the event feed and her record. If a cancellation, termination or job change has arrived, it stops and the plan is revised.

I approve the plan. I re-checked the live state and it matches the findings: there is still only one event (seq 1, HIRE), and nothing new has arrived. Workday has Nadia Rahman (E1023) as Active, starting 2026-11-04, with no work email, no rehire or conversion links and empty notes. The business date is now 2026-11-02 00:28. Her manager, Jordan Carter, has an active finance profile on CC-1000.

- **Every system is covered:** Finance (profile with cost center CC-1000 and Jordan Carter as expense approver), ITSM (equipment order), Identity (account plus the three birthright groups) and Workday (email write-back and both onboarding tasks). Legal needs nothing because there is no hold, and no irreversible steps are involved.
- **No access before the start date:** the account and groups wait until 2026-11-04. Before creating anything, the plan re-reads the event feed and her worker record, and stops if a termination or job change has come in. Setting up the finance profile and ordering equipment before the start date grants no access.
- **Ordering is right:**
  - The "Provision equipment" task is marked complete only after the equipment order is confirmed, which is when that task counts as done.
  - The email goes back to Workday only after the account exists.
  - "Create accounts and email" is marked complete only after the email shows in Workday.
  - The plan treats the resulting contact-change event as our own write-back, not a new case.
- **Policy checks pass:** the three groups (All-Staff, VPN-Users, Eng-Git) are not privileged and the segregation-of-duties check is clean. None of the rehire or conversion policies apply.
- **Duplicate protection:** every create has an idempotency key tied to the case. On a timeout or error, the plan re-reads before retrying, and it reuses an existing account if one appears. Nothing in her notes is acted on, since they are empty.

One small gap is that same-person matching rests on names, because there's no way to search by government ID token. With no rehire or conversion fields set and no matching accounts, that doesn't justify asking HR to confirm her identity.
